name: Slovenia
origin_test: Slovene emigrant (slovenski izseljenec) and their descendant in the direct line
instrument: Zakon o državljanstvu Republike Slovenije (uradno prečiščeno besedilo) (ZDRS-UPB2), Uradni list RS, št. 24/2007, item 1211
quote_original: Pristojni organ lahko, če je to v skladu z nacionalnim interesom, po prostem preudarku sprejme v državljanstvo Republike Slovenije slovenskega izseljenca in njegovega potomca do četrtega kolena v ravni črti, če dejansko živi v Republiki Sloveniji vsaj eno leto pred vložitvijo prošnje, če ima urejen status tujca in če izpolnjuje pogoje iz 1., 4., 5., 6., 7., 8., 9. in 10. točke prvega odstavka 10. člena tega zakona.
quote_translation: The competent authority may, if it is in accordance with the national interest, at its free discretion admit to citizenship of the Republic of Slovenia a Slovene emigrant and his descendant up to the fourth degree in the direct line, if he has actually lived in the Republic of Slovenia for at least one year before lodging the application, if his status as an alien is regulated and if he meets the conditions of points 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 of the first paragraph of Article 10 of this Act.
basis: ZDRS art. 12(1). The qualifying person is a *slovenski* izseljenec — an emigrant identified as Slovene, not merely a person who left Slovenia — and the provision nowhere requires that the emigrant ever held Slovenian citizenship. The contrast is internal: art. 12(2), the very next paragraph, deals separately with a person who LOST Slovenian citizenship by release or renunciation. Reading para 1 as a former-citizen rule would make para 2 redundant, so para 1 is the origin limb. The ceiling is on the face of the text: 'do četrtega kolena v ravni črti'.
notes: maximum_degree 4 is stated, not inferred, but the unit is Slovenian 'koleno' counted downward from the emigrant, so the fourth koleno is the emigrant's great-great-grandchild — one generation deeper than this schema's 'great_grandparent' vocabulary can name, which is why relations carries only ancestor_unspecified. Route is discretionary ('po prostem preudarku') and conditional on the national interest, and it still requires one year of actual residence with a regulated alien status, so route_kind is accelerated_naturalisation rather than citizenship. Text verified in the official consolidated version published in Uradni list RS 24/2007; the only later amendment, ZDRS-E (Uradni list RS 40/2017, item 2003, https://www.uradni-list.si/glasilo-uradni-list-rs/vsebina/2017-01-2003), was read in full and touches art. 13 only, adding a new second paragraph and renumbering — art. 12 is unchanged. pisrs.si, the successor consolidated database, is a single-page app returning a 11,805-byte shell for /pregledPredpisa?id=ZAKO13, so Uradni list is the fetchable authority.

name: Slovenia
origin_test: Slovene abroad within the meaning of art. 2 ZORSSZNM invoking the national interest on national grounds
instrument: Zakon o državljanstvu Republike Slovenije (uradno prečiščeno besedilo) (ZDRS-UPB2), Uradni list RS, št. 24/2007, item 1211
articles: 13. člen, drugi odstavek (tretji odstavek po ZDRS-E)
quote_original: Osebam iz 2. člena Zakona o odnosih Republike Slovenije s Slovenci zunaj njenih meja (Uradni list RS, št. 43/06), ki uveljavljajo korist države iz nacionalnih razlogov, ni treba izpolnjevati pogoja neprekinjenega prebivanja v Republiki Sloveniji na podlagi urejenega statusa tujca, pogoja 4. točke, če niso zavezanci za plačilo davkov v Republiki Sloveniji, pa tudi ne pogoja iz 9. točke prvega odstavka 10. člena tega zakona.
quote_translation: Persons referred to in Article 2 of the Act on Relations between the Republic of Slovenia and Slovenes Abroad (Uradni list RS, no. 43/06) who invoke the benefit to the state on national grounds need not meet the condition of uninterrupted residence in the Republic of Slovenia on the basis of a regulated alien status, nor the condition of point 4 if they are not liable for taxes in the Republic of Slovenia, nor the condition of point 9 of the first paragraph of Article 10 of this Act.
basis: ZDRS art. 13. Para 1 is the general national-interest naturalisation; this paragraph strips the residence requirement for one class only, defined by cross-reference to ZORSSZNM art. 2. That article, verified at https://www.uradni-list.si/glasilo-uradni-list-rs/vsebina/2006-01-1836, defines Slovenes outside Slovenia as 'pripadniki avtohtone slovenske narodne skupnosti v sosednjih državah' and 'Slovenci po svetu; to so zdomci in izseljenci', and art. 5(1) of the same Act calls them 'enakovreden del enotnega slovenskega naroda'. The test is peoplehood, so this is an origin route even though the citizenship act itself never says 'rod'.
notes: relations is empty on purpose: the operative test is membership of the Slovene nation, and no ancestor of any named degree has to be produced. Nothing in either instrument states a generational cutoff, so unlimited stays false and maximum_degree null — silence is not a ceiling and it is not an absence of one. ZDRS-E (Uradni list RS 40/2017) inserted a new second paragraph into art. 13 and renumbered this one as the third; the wording quoted is unchanged. The grant remains discretionary and requires a prior finding by the Government that the national-interest ground exists.

name: Slovenia
origin_test: of Slovene descent (slovenskega rodu / slovenskega porekla)
instrument: Zakon o odnosih Republike Slovenije s Slovenci zunaj njenih meja (ZORSSZNM), Uradni list RS, št. 43/2006, item 1836
quote_original: Status Slovenca brez državljanstva Republike Slovenije (v nadaljnjem besedilu: status Slovenca brez slovenskega državljanstva) lahko pridobi tisti posameznik: – ki je slovenskega rodu (slovenskega porekla);
quote_translation: The status of a Slovene without citizenship of the Republic of Slovenia (hereinafter: status of a Slovene without Slovenian citizenship) may be acquired by an individual: – who is of Slovene descent (Slovene origin);
basis: ZORSSZNM art. 59, first indent, with art. 60 ('Slovenski rod (slovensko poreklo) se dokazuje z izpiski iz rojstne matične knjige in drugimi ustreznimi dokazili') supplying the method of proof and art. 61 removing any territorial constraint on the ancestor: 'Ni pogoj, da predniki osebe, ki želi pridobiti status, izhajajo z območja, na katerem danes leži Republika Slovenija. Predniki osebe, ki želi pridobiti status, lahko izhajajo tudi iz zamejstva, zdomstva in izseljenstva.' — it is not a condition that the applicant's forebears came from the area that is Slovenia today. A state body decides what the applicant is; that is the pure form of the origin test.
notes: Recorded as residence_status because the instrument creates a status, not a nationality — but note what the status does and does not carry: art. 66 grants property rights on a par with citizens, priority over other non-EU foreigners in job competitions, university and archive access, but no residence right. Art. 69 extinguishes the status on acquisition of Slovenian citizenship, which is the same self-terminating shape as Karta Polaka and the Slovak certificate. Separately, arts. 71-76 run a state-organised repatriation for Slovenes from countries in severe crisis: art. 76(4) makes the repatriation decision operate as a temporary residence permit and art. 76(5) caps that status at 15 months. No generational limit appears anywhere in the Act, so maximum_degree is null and unlimited is false.

name: Croatia
origin_test: emigrant and their descendants, with an express ethnic-Croat limb for members of the Croatian people who emigrated from the wider former-state territory
instrument: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o hrvatskom državljanstvu, Narodne novine 102/2019 (25.10.2019.), članak 5., replacing art. 11 of the Zakon o hrvatskom državljanstvu (NN 53/91 et seq.)
quote_original: Iseljenik i njegovi potomci mogu prirođenjem steći hrvatsko državljanstvo iako ne udovoljavaju pretpostavkama iz članka 8. stavka 1. točaka 2. – 4. ovoga Zakona. Stranac koji je u braku s osobom iz stavka 1. ovoga članka može steći hrvatsko državljanstvo iako ne udovoljava pretpostavkama iz članka 8. stavka 1. točaka 2. – 4. ovoga Zakona. Iseljenik iz stavka 1. ovoga članka je osoba koja se prije 8. listopada 1991. godine iselila s područja Republike Hrvatske u namjeri da u inozemstvu stalno živi. Iznimno, iseljenik iz stavka 1. ovoga članka je i pripadnik hrvatskog naroda koji se iselio s prostora u sastavu bivših država u kojima se, u vrijeme iseljenja, nalazilo i područje današnje Republike Hrvatske.
quote_translation: An emigrant and his descendants may acquire Croatian citizenship by naturalisation even if they do not satisfy the requirements of Article 8(1)(2)-(4) of this Act. A foreigner married to a person referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article may acquire Croatian citizenship even if he does not satisfy the requirements of Article 8(1)(2)-(4) of this Act. An emigrant under paragraph 1 of this Article is a person who emigrated from the territory of the Republic of Croatia before 8 October 1991 with the intention of living permanently abroad. Exceptionally, an emigrant under paragraph 1 of this Article is also a member of the Croatian people who emigrated from territory within former states in which the area of today's Republic of Croatia was also located at the time of emigration.
notes: The 2020 change the brief asks about is this one: art. 11 as replaced by NN 102/2019, in force 1 January 2020. Read carefully, the article has two limbs and only the second is an origin test. Para 3 defines the emigrant territorially — someone who left Croatia before 8 October 1991 — which asks what happened, not what you are. Para 4 then extends 'emigrant' to a 'pripadnik hrvatskog naroda', a member of the Croatian people, who left any part of the former state that contained today's Croatia; that limb is ethnic on its face and is what earns origin_based true. Descendants are granted the same relief by para 1 with no degree named anywhere in the article, so maximum_degree is null. The article waives the requirements of art. 8(1)(2)-(4) — release from foreign citizenship, residence, and language and culture — but not art. 8(1)(5), the legal-order and security condition, which is why this is accelerated_naturalisation and not an entitlement to citizenship.
basis: Art. 11 of the Zakon o hrvatskom državljanstvu in the form given to it by art. 5 of the 2019 amending Act. The amending Act's own art. 1 recites the consolidated citation chain — NN 53/91, 70/91 ispravak, 28/92, 113/93 (Constitutional Court), 4/94, 130/11 and 110/15 — so the version fetched here is the operative text as at the 2019 amendment.

name: Croatia
origin_test: member of the Croatian people (pripadnik hrvatskog naroda) without residence in Croatia
instrument: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o hrvatskom državljanstvu, Narodne novine 102/2019 (25.10.2019.), članak 8., amending art. 16 of the Zakon o hrvatskom državljanstvu
quote_original: U članku 16. iza stavka 2. dodaje se stavak 3. koji glasi: »Iznimno od stavka 2. ovoga članka, dokaze o pripadnosti hrvatskom narodu ne mora priložiti osoba za čije je roditelje nesporno utvrđena pripadnost hrvatskom narodu.«.
quote_translation: In Article 16, after paragraph 2 a new paragraph 3 is added, reading: 'By way of exception to paragraph 2 of this Article, a person whose parents' membership of the Croatian people has been indisputably established need not attach evidence of membership of the Croatian people.'
basis: Art. 16 of the Zakon o hrvatskom državljanstvu is the standalone ethnic route — naturalisation of a member of the Croatian people who has no residence in Croatia — and art. 8 of the 2019 amending Act is the only part of it reproduced verbatim in a fetchable Narodne novine document. That paragraph is nonetheless dispositive on the character of the test: it speaks of 'dokazi o pripadnosti hrvatskom narodu', evidence of membership of the Croatian people, and relieves an applicant of producing it where the parents' membership is already established.
notes: This row is deliberately quoted from the amending provision rather than the base article. Narodne novine serves pre-1990s articles as an empty shell: https://narodne-novine.nn.hr/clanci/sluzbeni/1991_10_53_1170.html returns 13,293 bytes whose only content is 'Sadržaj je nedostupan', and the /clanci/sluzbeni/full/ variant returns a 2,264-byte page with an empty cached body, so the 1991 text of art. 16 cannot be cited to an official source. Modern NN articles do render server-side and are fine — 2019_10_102_2050 carries 18,713 characters of text. relations is ['parent'] because the parent is the only relative the quotable text names; art. 16 itself imposes no generational limit, hence maximum_degree null. Article 13(1)(3) of the same Act, also in the fetched document, lets a minor child naturalise where one parent acquires citizenship under art. 11(1) or art. 16, so both Croatian origin routes carry to children.

name: Romania
origin_test: none — descent from a person who held and lost Romanian citizenship
instrument: Legea cetăţeniei române nr. 21/1991, republished in Monitorul Oficial nr. 576 of 13 August 2010
quote_original: Persoanele care au dobândit cetăţenia română prin naştere sau prin adopţie şi care au pierdut-o din motive neimputabile lor sau această cetăţenie le-a fost ridicată fără voia lor, precum şi descendenţii acestora până la gradul III, la cerere, pot redobândi sau li se poate acorda cetăţenia română, cu posibilitatea păstrării cetăţeniei străine şi stabilirea domiciliului în ţară sau cu menţinerea acestuia în străinătate, dacă îndeplinesc condiţiile prevăzute la art. 8 alin. (1) lit. b), c) şi e).
quote_translation: Persons who acquired Romanian citizenship by birth or by adoption and who lost it for reasons not attributable to them, or from whom that citizenship was taken without their will, as well as their descendants up to the third degree, may on application regain or be granted Romanian citizenship, with the possibility of keeping their foreign citizenship and establishing their domicile in the country or maintaining it abroad, if they meet the conditions provided in Article 8(1)(b), (c) and (e).
basis: Art. 11 of Law 21/1991 as republished in 2010. The predicate is the ancestor's lost STATUS as a Romanian citizen, and the whole text of the Act was searched for an ethnic limb: 'origine', 'etnic' and 'naţionalit' appear nowhere in it. That is why origin_based is false, exactly as the brief anticipated — this is descent from a citizen, not a test of what the applicant is.
notes: The generational ceiling is stated and it is the one worth recording: 'descendenţii acestora până la gradul III'. Romanian civil-law degrees count downward from the person who lost the citizenship, so grade III is that person's great-grandchild, and the applicant's qualifying ancestor may be as remote as a great-grandparent — maximum_degree 3 from a stated ceiling, not from an enumeration that merely stops. The neighbouring art. 10 runs a parallel and shallower restoration, 'Cetăţenia română se poate acorda şi persoanelor care au pierdut această cetăţenie, precum şi descendenţilor acestora până la gradul II inclusiv', a second stated ceiling at grade II. Source note: legislatie.just.ro, the usual Romanian legislative portal, drops the socket for every request from this environment under both Bun and curl, and cetatenie.just.ro returns 503, so the text is cited to the Chamber of Deputies' legislative database. That database prints its own disclaimer, 'textele actelor normative nu au caracter oficial', so it is the parliament's copy of the republished text rather than Monitorul Oficial itself; monitoruloficial.ro was not reachable in a fetchable form.

name: Poland
origin_test: Polish origin (polskie pochodzenie): declared Polish nationality plus a Polish-nationality ancestor
instrument: Ustawa z dnia 9 listopada 2000 r. o repatriacji, Dz. U. 2000 nr 106 poz. 1118, consolidated text Dz. U. z 2026 r. poz. 90
quote_original: Za osobę polskiego pochodzenia, w rozumieniu niniejszej ustawy, uznaje się osobę deklarującą narodowość polską i spełniającą łącznie następujące warunki: 1) co najmniej jedno z jej rodziców lub dziadków albo dwoje pradziadków było narodowości polskiej; 2) wykaże ona swój związek z polskością.
quote_translation: A person of Polish origin, within the meaning of this Act, is deemed to be a person declaring Polish nationality and jointly satisfying the following conditions: 1) at least one of her parents or grandparents, or two great-grandparents, was of Polish nationality; 2) she demonstrates her connection with Polishness.
basis: Art. 5(1) of the Repatriation Act supplies the origin test; art. 4(1) supplies the consequence — 'Osoba przybywająca do Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej na podstawie wizy krajowej w celu repatriacji nabywa obywatelstwo polskie z mocy prawa z dniem przekroczenia granicy Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej.' — citizenship by operation of law on crossing the border on a repatriation visa, not a discretionary grant. Art. 5(3) adds that the ancestor's Polish nationality is treated as established where that ancestor confirmed belonging to the Polish Nation, in particular by cultivating Polish traditions and customs, which makes the test a national-character one rather than a documentary-citizenship one.
notes: This is the row the brief asks to be kept distinct from Karta Polaka, and the distinction is real: the Card is a status, this Act confers nationality itself, by operation of law. The two share a definitional shape — one parent or grandparent, or two great-grandparents — so maximum_degree 3 here is a stated ceiling in the same sense. What separates this route in practice is art. 9(1), which restricts the repatriation visa to people who before the Act's entry into force were permanently resident in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan or the Asian part of the Russian Federation, and whose deportation or exile to those territories was itself on account of Polish origin: 'Wiza krajowa w celu repatriacji może być wydana osobie, która spełnia łącznie następujące warunki: 1) jest polskiego pochodzenia; 2) (uchylony) 3) przed dniem wejścia w życie ustawy zamieszkiwała na stałe na terytorium obecnych Republiki Armenii, Republiki Azerbejdżanu, Gruzji, Republiki Kazachstanu, Republiki Kirgiskiej, Republiki Tadżykistanu, Turkmenistanu, Republiki Uzbekistanu albo azjatyckiej części Federacji Rosyjskiej; 4) ze względu na polskie pochodzenie ją samą lub jej wstępnych objęły deportacja lub zesłanie przez władze byłego Związku Socjalistycznych Republik Radzieckich na terytoria, o których mowa w pkt 3.'. So the origin test is open in principle and closed in geography. Art. 9(3) extends the visa to a spouse and to descendants to the fourth degree travelling with the qualifying person. Poland already sits in the corpus for descent and, per the sibling findings file, for Karta Polaka; this row is the third Polish instrument and must not be counted as new jurisdiction coverage.

name: Serbia
instrument: Zakon o državljanstvu Republike Srbije, 'Sl. glasnik RS' br. 135/2004, 90/2007 and 24/2018; art. 23 is reported to admit a 'pripadnik srpskog naroda' resident abroad without release from foreign citizenship
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: The Serbian gazette's own portal cannot be read by any non-browser client. https://www.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs/SlGlasnikPortal/eli/rep/sgrs/skupstina/zakon/2004/135/1/reg returns HTTP 200 with 13,015 bytes of Vue single-page shell yielding 317 characters of text, and EVERY path under /SlGlasnikPortal/ returns that identical 13,015-byte body — /api/reg/1, /reg/glasnik.css and a fabricated /prilozi/ path all return it, which is the Fedlex trap in a different language. The bundle reads its API base from window.env.VUE_APP_API_REG_DEV, and no script tag on the served index defines window.env, so the endpoint cannot be recovered from the shipped code. Of the plausible API hosts only reg.pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs resolves, and it returns 404 for /glasnik.css and for every ELI path tried. The National Assembly at www.parlament.gov.rs does serve real law PDFs under /upload/archive/files/cir/pdf/, but its adopted-laws index covers recent convocations only and carries nothing on citizenship. What is ambiguous is therefore not the law but the text: whether art. 23 in force today still reads as an entitlement for a member of the Serbian people, and whether the emigrant-descendant limb sits in art. 23 or in a neighbouring article, cannot be settled without a fetchable official text. No claim either way is recorded.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
instrument: Zakon o državljanstvu Bosne i Hercegovine, 'Službeni glasnik BiH'
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: No official BiH text could be reached. The Parliamentary Assembly at www.parlament.ba does serve a law database, but /law/SearchLaws is a POST form whose endpoint returns 404 to a direct POST at both /Law/SearchLaws and /law/SearchLaws, and the browsable consolidated-text list at /law/Read?categoryId=3 was walked in full across its five pages and contains no citizenship act — and the texts it does carry are labelled 'Neslužbeni prečišćeni tekst', unofficial consolidations, so they would be weak authority even if the act were there. www.sluzbenilist.ba and sllist.ba both respond, but the Službeni glasnik BiH is a subscription publisher and no free issue text was reachable. The specific question left open is whether the BiH act carries a facilitated-naturalisation clause for emigrants from Bosnia and Herzegovina and their descendants, and if so whether that clause names an ethnic limb or is purely territorial; neither the existence nor the wording of such a clause is asserted here.

name: Montenegro
instrument: Zakon o crnogorskom državljanstvu, 'Službeni list Crne Gore' br. 13/2008, published 26 February 2008
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: The act was located precisely and still could not be quoted. The gazette's index was walked to the right issue — https://www.sluzbenilist.me/registri?type=0&year=2008&page=3 lists 'broj 13/2008' at /registri/354793, whose contents page names 'Zakon o crnogorskom drzavljanstvu' at /propisi/334199 — but that document page carries metadata only: publication date, subject classification, and lists of implementing decisions and later amending acts. Its 141 kB body normalises to 1,997 characters of navigation text, contains no article of the law, no .pdf link, and no download route (/api/propisi/334199, /propisi/334199/tekst, /propisi/334199/pdf and /dokument/334199 all return the site's 404). The Pravno informacioni sistem at regis.sluzbenilist.me is an Angular shell. So the amendment history is visible — a Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama, a Zakon o dopuni and a Zakon o izmjeni i dopuni are all listed against it — while the operative text is not. Whether art. 12 grants naturalisation to an emigrant and descendants, and whether it states a degree limit, is left undetermined.

name: North Macedonia
instrument: Закон за државјанството на Република Македонија, 'Службен весник'
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: www.slvesnik.com.mk fails TLS verification: Bun's fetch, and therefore the quote gate, returns 'unable to verify the first certificate' on every request because the host serves an incomplete certificate chain. This is the same failure mode already recorded for mevzuat.gov.tr and resmigazete.gov.tr in the Turkish pass. curl accepts the chain, but a row cited to a host the gate cannot reach is a row nobody can re-verify, so nothing is claimed. The open question is the wording and generational reach of the emigrant clause said to sit at art. 8 or nearby, and in particular whether it names 'иселеник' territorially or reaches ethnic Macedonians who never lived in the state.

name: Albania
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: qbz.gov.al, the Centre for Official Publications, is an Angular front end over an Alfresco repository and returns the same 4,274-byte splash-screen shell (400 characters of text) for every path, including the ELI-shaped /eli/ligj/2020/07/16/113-2020. Its main bundle exposes only the generic Alfresco REST surface — /api/-default-/public/search/versions/1 and friends — so a document can be fetched only by an Alfresco node id that the app obtains at runtime; the ids are not derivable. www.parlament.al, the Assembly, does not complete a connection from this environment at all. What is undetermined is whether Law 113/2020 retains a naturalisation route for a person of Albanian origin, on what proof, and with what generational reach.

name: Moldova
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: legis.md, the State Register of Legal Acts and the only official consolidated source, returns HTTP 403 to every request from this environment — both the site root and /cautare/getResults — with a 5.6-8 kB challenge body that normalises to 84 characters. No alternative official Moldovan publisher was reachable. Worth flagging for whoever retries: the Moldovan provisions in this family are recognition rules keyed to birth on the territory and to deportation or refuge from it, so the likely outcome is an origin_based false row of the same shape as Romania's, not an ethnic route. That expectation is not a finding and no row is claimed on it.

name: Greece
instrument: ν. 3284/2004 Κώδικας Ελληνικής Ιθαγένειας, άρθρο 10; ν. 2790/2000; ν. 4735/2020
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: Greece has a genuine and substantial origin route for ομογενείς and it remains unquotable, for two blockers already documented in the European pass of this project. First, www.et.gr redirects to et.gr, which redirects to a bare IP address whose certificate cannot validate, so the National Printing House's search front end is unreachable to every client including a browser; ΦΕΚ PDFs are obtainable only by reconstructing blob URLs from the search app's bundle. Second, ΦΕΚ are printed in two columns, so pdftotext -layout interleaves them and no multi-line quote survives, and pre-2010 issues carry no Unicode mapping at all, extracting as ISO-8859-7 bytes rendered as Latin-1. Article 10 of the Code, 'Πολιτογράφηση ομογενών που διαμένουν στο εξωτερικό', requires no residence in Greece and turns on consular documentation of the applicant's ιδιότητα ως ομογενούς; ν. 2790/2000 art. 1(3) has a committee establish η ελληνική καταγωγή as a finding of fact. Neither can be cited to a fetchable official URL, so no row is claimed.

name: Bulgaria
instrument: Закон за българското гражданство, ДВ бр. 136/1998, art. 15 and §2 of the Additional Provisions
basis: cannot_determine — no fetchable official instrument; see notes for exactly what blocked it and what remains open.
notes: Not a gap in the law — a gap in reachable authority, plus a scoring problem in the existing corpus that is worth more than this row's absence. justice.government.bg/home/normdoc/2134446592, the URL the compiled corpus cites for the Bulgarian-origin route, fails TLS verification under Bun with 'unable to verify the first certificate', so the atlas's own source for that row cannot be re-fetched by the quote gate. dv.parliament.bg responds but its showMaterialDV.jsp pages carry only a few hundred characters, and www.parliament.bg/bg/laws returns a 4.3 kB shell. Separately and more importantly: data/compiled/citizenship_routes.json records bulgaria-bulgarian-origin-naturalization with descent.origin_based = false. 'Лице от български произход' is an explicitly ethnic test and should be true under the rule this batch applies. name: Hungary

notes: njt.hu, the National Legislation Database, drops the socket on every request from this environment under Bun's fetch — the same transport failure as legislatie.just.ro — so the consolidated text is unreachable. magyarkozlony.hu IS reachable and its PDFs extract cleanly, and its archive was walked back to 2010 by binary search over the paging index; the /dokumentumok/<hash>/letoltes endpoint serves real gazette PDFs with text layers. But 2010. évi XLIV. törvény, the amendment that created simplified naturalisation, was not found in Magyar Közlöny issues 85 through 95 of 2010, all of which were downloaded and searched for 'a magyar állampolgárságról szóló 1993. évi LV. törvény', and the search was stopped there rather than continued blind. The route is real and the wording of 4. § (3) — an applicant whose ancestor was a Hungarian citizen OR who makes Hungarian descent probable — is what the brief asks about, but it is not asserted from an unread document. Also worth recording: the corpus route hungary-citizenship-by-parent-or-simplified-origin cites an embassy page and a government hub rather than the Act, and scores origin_based false, which the 'valószínűsíti magyarországi származását' limb contradicts.
